questions.q: A mid-cycle surge in luteinising hormone occurs after sustained high estradiol secretion by the dominant follicle. What is the principal immediate ovarian event triggered by this surge?
options: Ovulation and luteinisation of the ruptured follicle
Suppression of progesterone secretion by the corpus luteum
questions.explain: Sustained high estradiol switches to positive feedback on the hypothalamic-pituitary axis, producing the LH surge. The surge triggers ovulation and initiates luteinisation of the remaining follicular cells.

questions.q: If fertilisation does not occur, what is the main endocrine event that initiates menstruation at the end of the luteal phase?
options: Regression of the corpus luteum with falling progesterone and oestrogen
An abrupt increase in hCG secretion
questions.explain: Without embryonic hCG rescue, the corpus luteum regresses. Falling progesterone and oestrogen lead to endometrial breakdown and menstruation.

questions.q: Which pituitary hormone primarily stimulates granulosa-cell proliferation and aromatase activity during follicular development?
questions.explain: FSH acts on granulosa cells to promote follicular growth and aromatase expression, allowing conversion of theca-derived androgens to oestrogens.

questions.q: Under the influence of progesterone after ovulation, the endometrium enters which phase?
questions.explain: Progesterone from the corpus luteum converts the oestrogen-primed endometrium into a secretory lining suitable for implantation.

questions.q: At ovulation, the human secondary oocyte is normally arrested at which meiotic stage?
questions.explain: The primary oocyte completes meiosis I shortly before ovulation. The secondary oocyte begins meiosis II and arrests at metaphase II until fertilisation.
